origin.trigger: Supervisor question: throughput trails FlashAttention transformers; did the Triton work on Mamba pay off?
origin.verified_answer: No Triton kernel ever executed. scan_triton.py / tfla_triton.py had one call site in the dead mamba_block_v2.py and were deleted in 37f7964; scan_interface.py:28 sets TRITON_AVAILABLE = False. The misleading artefacts are root test_triton_fix.py, the unused triton>=2.1.0 requirement, and the name TFLA (Tiled Flash Linear Attention).

measured_baseline.source: job 2561023, batch 4, bf16, H100, random weights, 14A-7 protocol
measured_baseline.verdict: Memory parity achieved (7.09 vs 7.15 GB where the old hybrid needed 42 GB). Wall-clock is 4-5x behind with flat, near-equal exponents: no crossover in the measured range.

hypothesis.primary: ssd_interface.py:169-190 carries chunk state in a Python `for ci in range(nc)` loop. At mamba3_chunk_size=64 and seqlen 16384, nc=256; with 9 Mamba-3 layers that is 2304 sequential iterations per forward, each launching several small CUDA kernels.
hypothesis.amdahl_caveat: 3 of 12 layers are mLSTM on pure-PyTorch TFLA and no Mamba kernel touches them. The ceiling on any SSD-only fix is 1/(1 - mamba3_time_fraction) and is UNMEASURED until E0-A.
hypothesis.status: UNVERIFIED — E0 exists to test this, not to assume it.

pre_registered.R1: Equivalence gate: rel-max-err <= 1e-4 vs the current operator in fp32, and agreement with ssd_sequential_reference (fp64) no worse than the current operator. A cu_seqlens boundary mismatch is an automatic fail.
pre_registered.R2: Memory outranks speed: any change whose peak memory exceeds the Transformer's at any measured length is rejected as a default, regardless of speedup.
pre_registered.R3: Adoption bar: >= 1.25x faster at >= 2 measured sequence lengths and nowhere more than 5% slower, else recorded as a null and reverted.
pre_registered.R4: Predict first: each phase records expected direction and magnitude before submission; wrong predictions are recorded beside the number.
pre_registered.R5: Honest framing: wall-clock parity is engineering, not a research contribution. If E0-F's bound says parity is unreachable, that bound is the deliverable and E3 is not attempted.

predictions.E0: Inter-chunk loop > 50% of Mamba-3 layer time at 16384; mLSTM 20-40% of model time; unfused attention slower than our scan at 16384.
predictions.E1: chunk_size 64->256 gives 1.5-2.5x at 16384 for < 1.5 GB extra; torch.compile < 1.3x and may fail by unrolling the nc loop.
predictions.E2: 2-4x on the Mamba-3 layers at 16384; the binding risk is R2 (memory), not correctness.

2026-09-25: E0 COMPLETE (jobs 2579631, 2579642). Scan is 67.5% of the forward at L=16384; Amdahl bound 4.50x vs a 4.14x gap. E0-D decisive: unfused attention is 16.8x slower at 8192 and OOMs at 16384, so the deficit is kernel engineering, not algorithm. Two pre-registered predictions WRONG: chunk_size is a U-curve peaking at 128 (1.40x, not monotonic 1.5-2.5x), and torch.compile gave 4.28x at L=2048 (predicted <1.3x), cutting the gap to 1.25x. Neither is adoptable until R1/R2 are checked; 2579642 timed out compiling L=16384 (FE4 as predicted).

2026-09-25: E1 COMPLETE (job 2580198). R1 PASSED on GPU incl. torch.compile (logits 3.0e-05 vs 1e-4 tol). CROSSOVER FOUND: compiled+chunk128 at L=16384 is 122.68 ms vs FlashAttention's 163.86 ms = 1.34x FASTER at memory parity (7.169 vs 7.152 GB); top-of-ladder latency exponent 0.47 ours vs 1.20 attention. chunk_size=128 adopt (>=1.25x at 5/7 lengths); torch.compile adopt as inference-time opt-in (R2: +17 MB over the Transformer, permitted only because compile is off by default). ANOMALY: compiled cs=64 and cs=128 time identically at 4096/8192 (1 us apart) while uncompiled differ 45% -- shared Inductor cache suspected; follow-up job isolates caches and prints the effective chunk size. RECOMMEND DROPPING E2 and E3: the gap they were justified by is closed.

2026-09-25: 2026-09-25: job 2582482 (2h TIMEOUT, partial). Part A RESOLVED the anomaly: chunk_size always reached the operator (both arms printed effective_chunk_size); the 1us match was a SHARED Inductor cache serving both arms one slow kernel at L=4096. Isolated caches made the same points 21-30% faster. Larger finding: within one process, shapes compiled later measure worse (3.04x at L=512 -> 1.02x at L=4096), so EVERY compiled number depends on what else was compiled beside it -- the 1.34x headline at L=16384 is UNCONFIRMED and must be re-measured. Part B: first training numbers ever taken (chunk128 ~1.45x at +6.5% memory; compile 3.04x at 512 collapsing to 1.02x at 4096) but the Transformer reference row never ran, so no training claim is available. Both wrappers now isolate caches; new profile_e1_confirm_h100.sh runs one shape per process.

2026-09-25: E1-E CONFIRMED (job 2582775, one shape per process, isolated caches, no timeout). Headline HOLDS: 122.90 ms vs FlashAttention's 164.85 ms at L=16384 = 1.34x faster at +0.24% memory, reproducing the contaminated run to 0.2%. NEW: also 1.15x faster at L=8192 (62.09 vs 71.26) where the contaminated run said 0.80x BEHIND. CORRECTION: the 0.47 exponent was an artefact of a too-slow contaminated 8192 point; clean exponents are ours 0.985 vs attention 1.210 -- our latency is linear, attention's is not. TRAINING with the Transformer reference at last: compile+chunk128 cuts the deficit from 5.86x to 2.71x at L=2048 and 8.74x to 1.23x at 1024, and compile LOWERS training memory. LIMITATION: memory parity is an INFERENCE claim only -- training uses 1.59x the Transformer's memory even compiled. Also: the standing '8x slower training' figure does not reproduce (measured 5.86x).

The wrapper defaulted to the 13D checkpoint + hybrid_150m_v2_rrg, the INCUMBENT, which has no mamba3 layer, so mamba3_chunk_size was set and never read. ROUGE-L 0.18358 vs the reference 0.1836 was a perfect tie because the knob was disconnected, not because it does nothing; the log said 'TRAINED with None' throughout. Fixed three ways: evaluate_report_generation.py now RAISES on a chunk_size override for a config with no mamba3 layer; the wrapper defaults to h100_report_gen_m3_tower13d_s42 + hybrid_150m_m3_rrg; and it decodes both arms in one job so they differ by exactly one setting.
